text: This lab pulls together everything from this chapter into one realistic Script Include: a method that takes a starting date and a number of days, computes a due date, builds a readable label describing it, and returns the whole thing as JSON so any caller can use it.

Script Includes are typically written as a single function wrapping a class-like object, using var at this outer level the way real ServiceNow code conventionally does, even in scripts written today. The method we're building, buildDueDateLabel, takes a starting GlideDateTime and a number of days as its two arguments.

Inside the method, we copy the starting GlideDateTime into a new one before calling addDaysUTC, because GlideDateTime objects are mutable - modifying the original directly could quietly change a value the caller still needs. addDaysUTC does the date math in UTC, which is the timezone-safe way to move a date forward, unlike native Date math.

Next, native string methods and a template literal build a short, readable label. Split pulls just the date portion out of the display value, and the template literal assembles the final label far more readably than concatenating with plus signs would.

Finally, the method builds a plain result object and returns it through JSON.stringify, so any caller - a Scripted REST API, a GlideAjax response, a log statement - gets back one predictable, parseable string. Calling the method and logging the result shows the full round trip: a JSON string out, parsed back into a real object to read a single property off it.

Across this one method: var and let used at the right scope, GlideDateTime instead of native Date for anything touching a real date, string methods and template literals for formatting, and JSON.stringify to hand back a structured result. That's every topic from this chapter, working together.
That closes Chapter 2. Chapter 3 moves to GlideRecord itself, starting with what GlideRecord actually does when you query the database.
